title: Prove at most 4g-3 full-mass destination channels at n = 2^g-1 (no new κ)
body:
## Result

Scoped written proof with an exact finite certificate. No new κ, precision invoice or supplier claim.

In PR628's balanced dirty word, Philippe Van Velzen's #2177 (`research/leaf-destination-transport-bound`, PROOF3) bounds the number of maximum-mass leaf-destination channels at one cut and register by 2F(floor(n/2)), but only when n+1 is not a power of two. For n = 2^g−1 it gives only census values (4g−3 for g = 3..7). This PR proves the excluded case:

**For n = 2^g−1, g ≥ 3, both orientations, at any cut and register, at most 4g−3 channels have mass g−1.** Hence

```
E_k(2^g−1) ≤ k(g−1) − max(0, k − (4g−3))
```

Before this, M1 (E_k ≤ k(g−1)) was the only proved bound at these sizes. The count is attained for g = 3..6 (9, 13, 17, 21) by exact check, so E_k(2^g−1) = k(g−1) for k ≤ 4g−3 at those sizes. Attainment for all g is not proved.

The new step is the pairing in PROOF.md case 5. The ceil half V = 2^(g−1) has floor log H. Bounding its (V,V') channels and V′'s internal channels separately by M3 gives 6 extra channels. Through #2177's Corollary I, they number A + 2c′. The sign-minus V′ has c′ ≤ 1, and when c′ = 1 the mirrored cut lies in V's first two phases, where A ≤ 1. So the total is at most 3, and 2F(b) + 3 = 4g−3. Lemma G (two full-scratch exits in a power-of-two call) and Lemma P2 (where mass-h channels occur in a power-of-two call) are derived from #2177's lemmas.

## Evidence and reproduction

`verify.py` (standard library, about 23 s) checks the following exactly in the free algebra, over every cut, register and injection:
- the word generator equals #2177's pinned `check2.gen` for n = 1..64, both signs;
- Lemma G for h = 1..5 and Lemma P2 for h = 2..5;
- every per-phase class bound of the proof table and the exact maximum 4g−3 for g = 3..6;
- two controls: a bound of 4g−4 is rejected, and the ceil-half split mutation breaks the bounds at n = 7, 15, 31.

From the repository root (local interpreter CPython 3.12 at `~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12`):

```sh
python3.12 -B research/all-ones-full-mass-channels/verify.py
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/all-ones-full-mass-channels
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/all-ones-full-mass-channels --check-source-history
```

Local results: `PASS_ALL_ONES_FULL_MASS_CHANNELS`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=partial` (23.9 s), and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES` for commit `ce9a4bf8233df1f0488cad8f74f940d08f88c565`.

## Limitations

- The upper bound is proved for all g ≥ 3. Attainment is a finite check for g = 3..6 only; #2177's census reports g = 7.
- The proof cites #2177's Theorem 1 case table, Corollary I, Lemmas L1 and X, and PROOF3's Lemma F and M3 source-dirty argument as premises. It does not re-verify them.
- Lower mass levels, conjecture C1, E_∞ at these sizes, internal leaf intermediates, correlated or rounded errors, and κ are not covered. No independent human or formal proof-kernel review.
- Card `uniform-transfer-audit`, with scope changed to this transport sub-question. It does not discharge any of the five selected-record assumptions.

## Open next questions

- Attainment of 4g−3 for every g: an explicit cut and register family, like #2177 Theorem 2.
- The largest number of mass H−1 channels at one cut. It is still census-only. `leaf-omega-profile` (#2735) fixes it only at the Omega cut of n = 2^h. Conjecture C1 remains open.

## Related open work

- #5931 (open) studies completed-target defect coefficients of dirty commutator trees with changed topology, in the same PR2067 independent-defect lineage. It is a different object and quantity (endpoint coefficient, not interior-cut channel counts), so no numbers are shared.

No other open PR studies leaf-destination channel counts. Merged predecessors: #2177 (model, M1–M3, census), #2735 (fixed Omega-cut profile for n = 2^h; different sizes and a fixed cut), #2067 (endpoint accumulation).
